# Selected target: complete Theorem 1

Source: this run's original.pdf, Theorem 1 on page 2, with the standing conventions and solution class on pages 2–3. The entire source paper, including its supplied proof, is checked-source.md.

The time grid in scheme (2) is \(\tau=T/L\), \(t_n=n\tau\), with \(L\) a positive integer and \(n=0,\ldots,L\). The maximum in Theorem 1 is over all these grid points. For fixed \(T>0\), \(0<\gamma\le1\) and \(R>0\), its \(C,\tau_0>0\) depend only on \(T,\gamma,R\) and are uniform over the specified initial-data ball and all grids with \(\tau\le\tau_0\). The theorem is for the displayed time-semidiscrete update without a spatial cutoff.

The following is the complete source statement and its standing context, transcribed from pages 2–3.

## 2 The scheme and the main result

Use normalized measure \(dx/(2\pi)\) on \(\mathbb T=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)\); changing to unnormalized \(L^2\) only changes constants. Write \(S_t=e^{-t\partial_x^3}\), so that \(\widehat{S_tf}(k)=e^{itk^3}\widehat f(k)\). Let \(P_0\) be the mean, \(P=I-P_0\), and define \(D^{-1}=\partial_x^{-1}\) with multiplier \((ik)^{-1}\) for \(k\ne0\) and zero at zero. Set \(D^{-2}=(D^{-1})^2\). Write
\[
\widehat f(k)=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}f(x)e^{-ikx}\,dx
\quad\hbox{and}\quad
\|f\|_{H^s}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}\langle k\rangle^{2s}|\widehat f(k)|^2,
\qquad \langle k\rangle=(1+k^2)^{1/2}.
\]
Spaces are the completions of trigonometric polynomials in these norms, with negative spaces interpreted as distributions. Orthogonality gives the normalized \(L^2\) identity for polynomials and hence for their completions. For mean-zero functions and \(s\ge0\), \(\|f\|_{\dot H^s}\le\|f\|_{H^s}\le2^{s/2}\|f\|_{\dot H^s}\); for \(s<0\), \(2^{s/2}\|f\|_{\dot H^s}\le\|f\|_{H^s}\le\|f\|_{\dot H^s}\). Real-valued means \(\widehat f(-k)=\overline{\widehat f(k)}\). All time suprema concern continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema. The exact solution is the unique real mean-zero \(C([0,T];H^\gamma)\) solution obtained by smooth approximation, and satisfies the equation distributionally. The constants \(C_M\) may change from line to line and depend on \(\gamma,T,M\), but are uniform in \(n,\tau\) and spectral support.

The equation is
\[
u_t+u_{xxx}=\tfrac12\partial_x(u^2),\qquad u(0)=u_0. \tag{1}
\]
The fixed scheme is \(u^0=u_0\) and
\[
u^{n+1}=S_\tau u^n+F_\tau(u^n)+H_\tau(u^n),\qquad \tau=T/L, \tag{2}
\]
where
\[
\begin{aligned}
F_\tau(f)&=\tfrac16 P[(S_\tau D^{-1}f)^2]-\tfrac16 S_\tau P[(D^{-1}f)^2],\\
H_\tau(f)&=\tfrac13 P[(S_\tau D^{-1}f)D^{-1}F_\tau(f)]
+\tfrac{\tau}{9}(S_\tau D^{-1}f)P_0(f^2)\\
&\quad-\tfrac1{54}\left[S_{\tau-s}D^{-1}[(S_sD^{-1}f)^3]\right]_{s=0}^{s=\tau}\\
&\quad-\tfrac1{27\tau}\left[S_{\tau-s}D^{-2}[(S_{s-\tau}D^{-2}F_\tau(f))(S_sD^{-1}f)]\right]_{s=0}^{s=\tau}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the scheme of [1, Eq. (1.4)], without a spatial frequency cutoff.

**Theorem 1 (Logarithm-free convergence).** Let \(T>0\), \(0<\gamma\le1\), and \(R>0\). For real, mean-zero \(u_0\in H^\gamma(\mathbb T)\) with \(\|u_0\|_{H^\gamma}\le R\), there are \(C,\tau_0>0\), depending only on \(T,\gamma,R\), such that the scheme (2) satisfies
\[
\max_{0\le n\le L}\|u(n\tau)-u^n\|_{L^2}\le C\tau^\gamma
\qquad\text{whenever }\tau=T/L\le\tau_0.
\]

The periodic KdV bounds of Babin–Ilyin–Titi control the exact flow on the initial-data ball. The continuous estimates of [1, Proposition 3.4 and Lemma 7.2] will be used in the stability proof. The logarithmic convergence theorem itself is not used. For the exact twisted solution \(v(t)=S_{-t}u(t)\), set
\[
M=1+\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|v(t)\|_{H^\gamma}.
\]
The source statements and the sign transformation giving a bound for \(M\) are recorded below in Section 2.1. No convergence theorem for the numerical scheme is used as an input. Intermediate constants may depend on \(M,\gamma,T\), but never on the timestep or a Fourier support bound.

<!-- PDF page 3 -->

### 2.1 The exact KdV flow

The source [2, Theorems 4.2–4.3, 5.1, 6.3–6.5] treats \(U_t=UU_x+U_{xxx}\) on the same torus, with normalized measure and mean-zero homogeneous Sobolev norms. Theorem 4.2 bounds its Galerkin flows on \([0,T]\) in \(\dot H^s\) by a constant depending only on \(s,T,\|U_0\|_{\dot H^s}\) and an upper bound for \(\|U_0\|_2\). Theorem 4.3 gives a distributional limiting solution with the same bound. Theorems 5.1 (\(s>1/2\)) and 6.3 (\(0<s\le1/2\)) give its uniqueness, \(C([0,T];\dot H^s)\) regularity and continuous dependence. Theorem 6.4 covers \(s=0\), and Theorem 6.5 with \(\theta=0\) states that, for two flows whose initial \(L^2\) norms sum to at most \(B\),
\(\sup_{[0,T]}\|U-\widetilde U\|_2\le C(T,B)\|U_0-\widetilde U_0\|_2\).
Together these results specify the continuous flow and the uniform bounds needed here.

Define \(u(t,x)=-U(t,-x)\). Then \(u_t=-U_t\), \(u_x=U_x\), \(u_{xxx}=U_{xxx}\) at \((t,-x)\), and consequently \(u_t+u_{xxx}=uu_x\). Fourier coefficients become \(\widehat u(k)=-\widehat U(-k)\), preserving every Sobolev norm, reality and zero mean. This transforms the source equation to (1). The norm comparison above transfers all bounds to our \(H^\gamma\) norm. Hence there is \(A(T,\gamma,R)<\infty\) such that every smooth initial datum in the stated ball satisfies \(\sup_{[0,T]}\|u(t)\|_{H^\gamma}\le A\). The same bound holds for the limiting solution: for each finite set of frequencies pass to the limit in its finite norm sum, then take the supremum over finite sets. Thus \(M\le1+A(T,\gamma,R)\) uniformly. Continuous dependence in \(L^2\) is precisely the input used in the final density passage. No change of torus length or amplitude scaling is needed.


## Supplied proof route

The following sentences are transcribed from the supplied paper's abstract/introduction:

"The main estimate concerns the exact averaged cubic remainder. Retaining both ratios of its two oscillatory phases bounds the dual four-frequency multiplier by the reciprocal of the third largest frequency. A dyadic four-linear estimate sums this majorant without a logarithm and includes a mixed \(L^2\) endpoint. That endpoint controls the remainder at the numerical state without a numerical Sobolev bound. We then prove the full global estimate using the continuous trilinear bounds of Li and Wu, a stepwise residual calculation, low–high frequency stability, a restarted bootstrap, and density."

"In particular, the normal-form identity keeps both endpoints when the time interval is restarted, and its forcing term is estimated from the actual stepwise residual. A fixed-timestep approximation argument then removes the temporary smoothness used in the calculations."

The complete supplied proof, including all definitions, transformations, evolution equations, identities, estimates, experimental sections and bibliography, is retained in checked-source.md in original page order.
spec.conclusion: There exist C>0 and tau0>0, depending only on T,gamma,R and valid simultaneously on the whole stated initial-data ball, such that for every real mean-zero g in H^gamma(torus) with ||g||_{H^gamma}<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, the exact solution u_g (the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional KdV solution obtained by smooth approximation) and the unfiltered scheme u_g^0=g, u_g^{n+1}=Psi_tau(u_g^n) satisfy max_{0<=n<=L}||u_g(n tau)-u_g^n||_{L2}<=C tau^gamma. In particular this holds for the supplied u0, including n=0, without any spatial frequency cutoff.

argument.text: Define \(u(t,x)=-U(t,-x)\). Then \(u_t=-U_t\), \(u_x=U_x\), \(u_{xxx}=U_{xxx}\) at \((t,-x)\), and consequently \(u_t+u_{xxx}=uu_x\). Fourier coefficients become \(\widehat u(k)=-\widehat U(-k)\), preserving every Sobolev norm, reality and zero mean. This transforms the source equation to (1). The norm comparison above transfers all bounds to our \(H^\gamma\) norm. Hence there is \(A(T,\gamma,R)<\infty\) such that every smooth initial datum in the stated ball satisfies \(\sup_{[0,T]}\|u(t)\|_{H^\gamma}\le A\). The same bound holds for the limiting solution: for each finite set of frequencies pass to the limit in its finite norm sum, then take the supremum over finite sets. Thus \(M\le1+A(T,\gamma,R)\) uniformly. Continuous dependence in \(L^2\) is precisely the input used in the final density passage. No change of torus length or amplitude scaling is needed. More explicitly, the physical change u(t,x)=-U(t,-x) maps initial data g to source initial data -g(-x), so preserves the whole initial-data ball. The homogeneous-to-inhomogeneous inequalities follow coefficientwise from |k|<=<k><=sqrt(2)|k| for k!=0. For a continuous limiting flow the finite-frequency sums and then their supremum give the bound at each time, with the same constant. Apply the source pair bound after this isometry; it gives the stated C(T,B0) bound. Twisting by S_{-t} differentiates away -partial_x^3 and gives v'=B_t(v,v)/2. This proves all clauses of N001, for arbitrary data in the ball.

\(|h(s)|\le\tau^{-1}\int_0^\tau|\alpha||s-r|\,dr\le\tau|\alpha|\)

\[

Fix four nonnegative ell2 sequences, under temporary antecedent L1.  It suffices first to consider finitely supported sequences. Decompose into shells \(2^j\le|k|<2^{j+1}\), \(j\ge0\), and write \(Xshell_{r,j}\) for the \(\ell^2\) norm of the \(r\)th sequence on the \(j\)th shell. Fix an ordering of the four shell indices \(j_1\ge j_2\ge j_3\ge j_4\). A nonzero zero-sum interaction has \(j_1-j_2\le2\). For each fixed pair of smaller-shell frequencies, the remaining sum of the two larger-shell sequences is at most their \(\ell^2\) norm product by Cauchy–Schwarz, since one sequence is a translated reflection of the other. Sum the smaller frequencies in \(\ell^1\). A shell has at most \(2^{j+1}\) integer elements, so another Cauchy–Schwarz bound gives
\[
\sum_{a+b+c+d=0}\prod_{r=1}^4 x_{r,j_r}
\le C2^{(j_3+j_4)/2}\prod_{r=1}^4 Xshell_{r,j_r}.
\]
Since \(N_3\ge2^{j_3}\), the weight leaves \(C2^{-(j_3-j_4)/2}\). For \(q=j_1-j_2\in\{0,1,2\}\), extend the nonnegative sum by dropping the upper restriction on the smaller shells. The contribution is at most
\[
C\left(\sum_{J0} Xshell_{1,J0}Xshell_{2,J0-q}\right)
\left(\sum_{\ell\ge m}2^{-(\ell-m)/2}Xshell_{3,\ell}Xshell_{4,m}\right).
\]
The first factor is bounded by Cauchy–Schwarz. Writing \(r=\ell-m\), the second is at most
\[
\sum_{r\ge0}2^{-r/2}\|Xshell_3\|_{\ell^2}\|Xshell_4\|_{\ell^2}
=\frac{\|Xshell_3\|_{\ell^2}\|Xshell_4\|_{\ell^2}}{1-2^{-1/2}}.
\]
Sum over at most 24 orderings and three offsets. For arbitrary nonnegative sequences apply the finite bound to their restrictions to \(|k|\le m\). The infinite positive sum is the supremum of these finite sums, while the norms of the restrictions are bounded by the full norms. This proves the infinite statement without exchanging conditionally convergent sums. 
Restriction to a subset only decreases the nonnegative sum. Discharge L1 to obtain the universally quantified N003.

\]
Together with the stage bounds N005, this yields
\[
\sup_{I_n}\|F_n(t)\|_{H^{a_\gamma}}+\sup_{I_n}\|F_n(t)\|_{L^2}\le C_Mq_n,
\qquad\|z_n\|_{X(I_n)}\le C_M. 
\]
For the exact-data contribution, apply the product bound N005 to \(\partial_x(S_tF_n(t;w))\) and \(S_tF_n(t;w)\); use the stage bounds N005. Write \(A=F_n(t;w)\) and \(D=F_n(t)-A\). The exact-data term obeys

\[
\sup_{I_n}\|\mathcal B_t(F_n(t),F_n(t))\|_{L^2}\le C_Mq_n.
\]
Consequently N004 implies
\[
\sup_{I_n}\|Q_n(t)\|_{L^2}+\|W_n\|_{L^2}\le C_M\tau q_n. 
These are all asserted stage and endpoint-correction bounds.

\[
\sup_{I_n}\|Y_n\|_{L^2}\le C_Mq_n. 
\]
Since \(p_*>1\), the defect bounds just calculated–the defect bounds just calculated imply the important pair
\[
\|Y_n\|_{X(I_n)}\le C_Mq_n,\qquad
\sup_{I_n}\|Y_n\|_{H^{-p_*}}\le C_M\tau q_n. 
\]
For the first term in the exact formula for C_n, use the symmetric asymmetric J bound of N006 with ||F_n||_2<=C_M q_n from F001. The H^(-pstar) and derivative conclusions follow coefficientwise from Dinv and pstar>1, as in N006. This proves all clauses of N008. argument.text: Use H001 and a smooth datum in the ball. N001 gives its smooth exact twisted flow v and M. N007 gives continuous V agreeing with the numerical grid. Put e=v-V, I=[a,b], h=b-a<=1, starting at a grid point. Assume L1: 0<tau<=1 and E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1. Every intersected step has delta_n=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I. Summing the N009 increment bound over at most h/tau+1 steps gives sup_I||Res(t)-Res(a)||_2<=C_M(h+tau)(tau^gamma+E_I). The exact derivative identity is e'=B_t(e,v-e/2)-Res'. Apply N006 and N009 to get ||e||_X<=C_M(tau^gamma+E_I). Also ||V||_2<=||v||_2+1 and V'=B(V,V)/2+Res' give ||v||_X+||V||_X<=C_M. Continuity permits these statements across step interfaces.

For any \(t\in I\), define \(\mathcal F_I(t)=\int_a^t\mathcal B_s(e,v-e/2)\,ds\). The exact error identity is
\[
e(t)=e(a)+\mathcal F_I(t)-(\mathcal R(t)-\mathcal R(a)). 
\]
Choose a Fourier threshold \(N\ge2\) only in the proof. It is not part of the algorithm. The low frequencies satisfy
\[
\sup_{t\in I}\|P_{\le N}\mathcal F_I(t)\|_{L^2}\le C_MN^2hE_I. 
\]
For example \(\|\partial_x^{-1}P(fg)\|_{L^2}\lesssim\|f\|_{L^2}\|g\|_{L^2}\), followed by the two-derivative Bernstein bound, proves the error identity.

For high frequencies, the normal-form identity N006 gives, retaining *both* endpoints,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal F_I(t)
&=\tfrac13[\mathcal J_s(e,v-e/2)]_{s=a}^{s=t}
-\tfrac13C_{[a,t]}(e,v-e/2,V)-\tfrac16C_{[a,t]}(v,v,e)\\
&\quad+\tfrac13\int_a^t\mathcal J_s(\mathcal R',V)\,ds. 
\end{aligned}
\]
For an explicit verification put \(g=v-e/2\). Then \(e'=\mathcal B(e,g)-\mathcal R'\) and \(g'=\tfrac12\mathcal B(v,v)-\tfrac12\mathcal B(e,g)+\tfrac12\mathcal R'\).
In the differentiated terms of the normal-form identity N006, symmetry of \(\mathcal J\) gives \(C(e,g,g)-\tfrac12C(e,g,e)=C(e,g,V)\) because \(g-e/2=V\).
The remaining cubic term is \(\tfrac12C(v,v,e)\), and the forcing terms are
\(-\mathcal J(\mathcal R',g)+\tfrac12\mathcal J(e,\mathcal R')=-\mathcal J(\mathcal R',V)\).
Multiplication by \(-1/3\) yields exactly the normal-form expansion. The endpoint terms after \(P_{>N}\) are bounded by \(C_MN^{-1}E_I\) by the \(H^1\) bound for \(\mathcal J\) in the elementary bounds N006.
Here P_{<=N} denotes the multiplier 1_{|k|<=N}; its complement is P_{>N}. The low estimate uses N006's Dinv P product bound and the factor k^2<=N^2. F001 gives the differentiated equations, and N006 justifies the normal form piecewise: continuous interface endpoints cancel. The initial endpoint at a is retained even when e(a)!=0.

produces.statement: With mathcal F_I(t)=integral_a^t B_s(e,v-e/2)ds, e(t)=e(a)+mathcal F_I(t)-(Res(t)-Res(a)) and sup||P_{<=N}mathcal F_I||_2<=C_M N^2 h E_I. Exactly mathcal F_I(t)=(1/3)[J_s(e,v-e/2)]_a^t-(1/3)C_[a,t](e,v-e/2,V)-(1/6)C_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Res',V)ds. The high-output boundary terms are <=C_M N^(-1)E_I.

argument.text:
We spell out how the high-output trilinear terms are estimated. If all three inputs have frequencies at most \(N/3\), the output cannot exceed \(N\). Write \(Lo=P_{\le N/3}\) and \(Hi=I-Lo\). The telescoping expansion is
\(C(f_1,f_2,f_3)-C(Lof_1,Lof_2,Lof_3)=C(Hif_1,f_2,f_3)+C(Lof_1,Hif_2,f_3)+C(Lof_1,Lof_2,Hif_3)\).
The low-input term has no output above \(N\), and each projection contracts both components of \(X(I)\). For the specified high input, \(\|Hif_i\|_{H^{-p_*}}\le CN^{-p_*}\|f_i\|_2\). In the time-dependent trilinear bound N005, place the \(H^{-p_*}\) norm on that input. Bernstein gives
\[
\|P_{>N}C_I(f_1,f_2,f_3)\|_{L^2}
\le Ch\prod_j\|f_j\|_{X(I)}+CN^{-p_*}\prod_j\|f_j\|_{L^\infty(I;L^2)}. 
\]
Applying F001 to the middle two terms of the high-output trilinear estimate just derived yields \(C_Mh\tau^\gamma+C_M(h+N^{-p_*})E_I\).

The last term of the high-output trilinear estimate just derived requires the stepwise formula for \(\mathcal R'\) in the residual identity N009. On each intersected step it becomes a sum of
\[
-C(Y_n,z_n,V),\qquad-\tfrac12C(Y_n,Y_n,V),\qquad
-\tau^{-1}\int\mathcal J_s(W_n,V)\,ds.
\]
The first two are \(O(\tau q_n)\) by the time-dependent trilinear bound N005, with the negative norm on \(Y_n\), and F002, F001. The last is \(O(\tau q_n)\) by F001 and the \(L^2\) bound for \(\mathcal J\). Even for a partial final step this is a valid upper bound. Summing gives \(C_M(h+\tau)(\tau^\gamma+E_I)\). Combining these facts,
\[
\sup_{t\in I}\|P_{>N}\mathcal F_I(t)\|_{L^2}
\le C_M(h+\tau)\tau^\gamma+C_M(h+\tau+N^{-1}+N^{-p_*})E_I. 
\]
The projection names here are Lo=P_{<=N/3} and Hi=I-Lo. By N006 they commute with time derivatives and contract X. The middle two normal-form terms each contain e once, hence their products of L2 norms contribute E_I and products of X norms contribute tau^gamma+E_I, by F001. N005 applies with any selected high input in its negative-norm slot. In the forcing integrals use the stepwise identity N009, the two Y_n norms in N008 and the bounds on V in F001. The O(tau q_n) sum includes a possible partial last step.

argument.text:
Use successive blocks of \(\lfloor\delta/\tau\rfloor\) steps, whose lengths lie in \([\delta/2,\delta]\), with a possibly shorter final block. The number of blocks is at most \(2T/\delta+1\), independently of \(\tau\). Iterating F001, starting with \(e(0)=0\), yields
\[
\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|e(t)\|_{L^2}\le C_{M,\gamma,T}\tau^\gamma, 
\]
as long as the bootstrap bound is in force. By continuity, if \(\|e\|_{L^2}\) first reached one, the same block argument up to that time would give an upper bound \(C_{M,\gamma,T}\tau^\gamma\). Choosing \(\tau_0\) smaller so that this is less than \(1/2\) gives a contradiction. Hence the accumulated block estimate holds on all of \([0,T]\). The retained initial endpoint in F003 is estimated by \(E_I\) on each block, so the recurrence also applies when \(e(a)\ne0\).
Explicitly set K=ceil(2T/delta)+1 and B_0=0, B_{j+1}=2B_j+C_M' delta. Finite induction gives B_j=C_M' delta(2^j-1). The same bound covers a truncated final block because F001 includes partial last steps. Let C0=C_M' delta(2^K-1), and choose tau0<=min(1,delta/2) with C0 tau0^gamma<1/2; gamma>0 makes this possible. At a hypothetical first hitting time ||e||_2=1, all interval suprema up to and including that time are <=1 by continuity (N001,N007), so the same finite recurrence contradicts C0 tau^gamma<1/2. Thus the bound holds on all [0,T]. At grid points N007 and Airy unitarity give ||e(t_n)||_2=||u(t_n)-u^n||_2. All constants were chosen using the common bound before selecting a datum or a grid.

argument.text: For each fixed tau>0 the unmodified Psi_tau is continuous L2->L2. N006 gives Dinv:L2->H^1 and the H^1 algebra bound, so F_tau:L2->H^1 is continuous quadratic. The first H_tau term is a product of inverse derivatives, hence continuous. The second uses the bilinear mean P0(f^2), bounded by ||f||_2^2, times S_tau Dinv f. In the third term each endpoint cube (S_s Dinv f)^3 is a continuous H^1 product followed by Dinv. In the fourth, S_{s-tau} Dinv2 F_tau(f) and S_s Dinv f are H^1 factors, followed by Dinv2. All coefficients, including 1/tau, are finite at fixed tau. The Airy terms are continuous by unitarity. Thus every displayed term is continuous into L2, and all iterates are well-defined; their formulas preserve reality and zero mean. For fixed positive L and tau=T/L finite induction gives u_m^n->u^n in L2 at every grid point.
